skills.account-briefing-boards.1: Imagine if every pitch started with a briefing like this: four boards you can read in a minute. Addvery's four are on
skills.account-people-classifier.1: Who's at a company, what they do, and do they actually sell? Maybe that's over-engineering. Still: 57 people, 107 model calls, $0.003, and I only show counts.
skills.account-scrape-apify.1: Everyone at a company, their posts and their podcast transcripts, all public, and I never log into anyone's LinkedIn. Addvery cost $1.24 for 279 results.
skills.agent-view-generator.1: A plain Markdown copy of the site, plus /llms.txt, built from the same files as the pages, so it can't drift. 77 files so far, not live yet.
skills.brand-clone-tokens.1: Give it a company's live site and it pulls the real colours, fonts, spacing and motion, at four screen widths. That's where this site's look came from.
skills.brand-voice-posts-graded-blind.1: A company's voice written down as rules, and a judge that wrote none of the posts. My 5 posts met all 21 rules. The same AI without the rules met 12.
skills.build-in-public-feed.1: Every 30 minutes it read what I'd said, wrote a short post and asked the website to publish it. 10 posts went live without me asking.
skills.capture-rig.1: Four commands record my screen, webcam and mic, transcribe it all, and find any quote to the second. About 5 h 30 min of me so far.
skills.group.1: Find the right accounts and people
skills.hero.1: It looks costly, and it isn't. Most of it is skills and workflows, so I could do the same thing tomorrow for a new company in half the time.
skills.icp-grid-from-client-site.1: Four agents read a company's whole site and work out which customers it can actually prove it serves. For Addvery: 4 ICPs out of 12 case studies.
skills.lead-router.1: Every lead gets an ICP, a language and a tactic, with the reason written down. Rules settled 4 of my 12 fictional leads for free. The model isn't wired in yet.
skills.linkedin-wall-builder.1: Someone's public LinkedIn posts as one wall, word for word, images and all. Mine took 6.6 seconds and $0.19 for 94 posts.
skills.onepassword-batch.1: Every key a task needs, in one 1Password approval. Nothing gets printed, and no key moves while I'm recording. The whole scraping run went by with no key on screen.
skills.operator-attention-controls.1: Questions wait at one desk, one at a time, and after 15 minutes the session decides and says why. At 13:20 I closed every session by accident. They were back in 9 minutes.
skills.outbound-workflow-factory.1: One copy file per ICP goes in, every GetSales sequence comes out, message 1 already set to the one variable. All 36 took 7 minutes.
skills.publish-leak-scan.1: Before anything gets committed or published, it's scanned for API keys, banned terms, emails and phone numbers. The 19 clips got a frame checked every two seconds.
skills.research-desk.1: About four questions per list, then three wildcards who chase the biggest question nobody asked. That got me 27 reports, all indexed.
skills.spec-driven-agent-team.1: One charter says why and what. Every deliverable gets its own spec, its own session and a log of every call made without me. About 15 sessions, 739 commits, one day.
skills.stakeholder-landing-pages.1: Instead of one pitch for everyone, every decision-maker gets a page of their own, in their company's look. There are six.
skills.taste-grading-booth.1: I grade moments blind, one key each, with 30% locked away first so the rubric gets tested on my taste. 126 of 127 graded. The rubric's next.
skills.transcript-to-article.1: You talk, it writes a near-final article that still sounds like you, and you do the last 10%. Three of my articles started this way.
